messages.author: 97d82fedb7016adb
messages.subject: [stan-math] convention for Jacobians?
parts:
Hi!

I am confused by the convention in stan-math for Jacobians. Assume I have a function f(x) which produces m=1...M outputs from n=1...N inputs x_n. Then I would expect the Jacobian matrix to be a M x N matrix with the usual definition:

df_m/dx_n = J_m,n

This is in line with what is written in the arXiv paper on page 13. However, the implementation in

math/stan/math/rev/mat/functor/jacobian.hpp

returns the transpose of this matrix, i.e. I get a N x M matrix with elements J_n,m ... why is that? If so, then this is inconsistent with what is claimed to be the Jacobian on page 14.

Or did I read the code wrong? I am quite new to using stan-math, so please correct me here if I am wrong.

Thanks!

Sebastian

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] [stan-math] convention for Jacobians?
parts:
I'm sure that's my fault. I can never keep these things
straight.

According to this:

https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacobian_matrix_and_determinant

if f: R^N -> R^M, then the Jacobian should be M x N

But in

math/rev/mat/functor/jacobian.hpp

you're right that the return is N x M. I'm opening an issue:

https://github.com/stan-dev/math/issues/230

- Bob
